invariants.rule: schemas/config.schema.json can declare a field years before any code actually consumes it -- implementation.output_licence existed, documented, unused, until this run wired it into CaseBundle.output_licence_id and cli.py's legal command. Always check config.schema.json against real consumers (grep the field name in src/) before assuming a documented config field does anything.
evidence: src/cleanroom/legal/engine.py CaseBundle had no field for it until commit d7071c2

invariants.rule: Any pack field that cross-references other SPDX identifiers (e.g. EUPL-1.2.yml's compatible_licences) must have every entry checked against cleanroom.licence.spdx.KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS before being written -- a licence's own prose (e.g. 'GPL v2 and v3') does not itself specify the exact -only/-or-later SPDX id, so expanding it is this project's own mapping, not a claim the source text drew that precise distinction.

policies/licences/*.yml is a generic glob (policy.py's available_packs()/load_pack()) -- adding a new pack requires no code change and no hardcoded list update anywhere in src/, only narrative doc/test-count updates.

licence/discovery.py's confidence (high vs medium) is driven entirely by license-expression's own SPDX known_symbols table (licence/spdx.py's KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS), completely independent of whether a policies/licences/<id>.yml pack exists for that id.
evidence: verified directly: removing a pack does not change discover()'s confidence for an SPDX-recognised id

invariants.rule: A licence pack file existing only changes: (a) obligations surfaced by policy.py's evaluate(), (b) the legal-engine heuristics that call load_pack() (copyleft-driven distribution/linking/licence_obligations, patent_risk, trademark_risk, contractual_permissions). It never changes discovery confidence (see the discovery invariant above).
evidence: src/cleanroom/legal/engine.py: 7 load_pack() call sites enumerated and checked this run

invariants.rule: CaseBundle.jurisdiction holds the RAW MARKET CODE (gb/uk/us/fr/de/jp/eu), never the jurisdiction PACK ID (england-wales/usa-federal/...) -- jurisdiction/resolver.py's COUNTRY_TO_PACK maps one to the other but CaseBundle itself never stores the pack id.
evidence: found and fixed as a real bug in an earlier session pass (database_rights heuristic)

invariants.rule: A licence term with NO matching policy pack must be treated as UNKNOWN by every legal/engine.py heuristic that reads load_pack() results, never silently folded into the same branch as a term confirmed non-copyleft/non-restrictive. The shared _licence_terms_with_packs() helper is the correct pattern (used by _licence_obligations, _patent_risk, _trademark_risk, _contractual_permissions).
evidence: fixed this run in _distribution and _linking, which had NOT followed this invariant before

invariants.rule: osi_approved/fsf_libre on a licence pack must be verified against a real primary source (SPDX's own license-list-data JSON at raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/license-list-data, or the licence's own steward site e.g. opensource.org) before being written, never assumed from general recollection -- both fields were independently wrong-by-omission risks this run (EUPL-1.2 confirmed true/true; the 4 data licences confirmed false/not-present).
evidence: this run's WebFetch verification of etalab-2.0, DL-DE-BY-2.0, DL-DE-ZERO-2.0, EUPL-1.2, OGL-UK-3.0 against SPDX license-list-data and/or opensource.org

contradictions.description: _distribution() and _linking() in legal/engine.py silently returned GREEN_WITH_CONDITIONS for a licence term with no matching policy pack, identical to a term confirmed non-copyleft -- inconsistent with _licence_obligations/_patent_risk/_trademark_risk/_contractual_permissions, which all correctly report AMBER 'unknown to this tool' for the same missing-pack case via the shared _licence_terms_with_packs() helper.

assumptions.claim: Japan has no SPDX-recognised government/public-sector open-data licence identifier, so no licence pack analogous to OGL-UK-3.0/etalab-2.0/DL-DE-* can be built for it without fabricating an spdx_id.

US federal government works are public domain by statute (17 U.S.C. Sec. 105), not by a licence -- SPDX only has narrower agency-specific identifiers (NIST-PD, NASA-1.3, NTIA-PD), no general 'US government work' licence pack is the right shape here.
assumptions.supersededBy: The 'no general pack' framing was right but the earlier conclusion this therefore wasn't worth building was wrong: NIST-PD/NASA-1.3/NTIA-PD were built as three separate real packs. NASA-1.3 in particular is NOT a public-domain instrument -- it's a real, substantive, OSI-approved copyleft-shaped licence (contractor-authored NASA software can carry real copyright, unlike a pure civil-servant Sec. 105 work), which the earlier assumption's framing ('US federal works are public domain by statute') implicitly, incorrectly generalised to. See policies/licences/NASA-1.3.yml's header comment.

assumptions.claim: EUPL-1.2's Article 5 'Compatible Licence' escape hatch (merging into a larger work, then redistributing under a different named licence) is NOT modelled by legal/engine.py -- the engine only reads the pack's own copyleft field, so a project that genuinely exercised this clause may see an AMBER/RED finding that a human reviewer could resolve differently.
assumptions.supersededBy: Partially modelled now (commit d7071c2): CaseBundle.output_licence_id + _compatible_licence_overlap() cross-reference EUPL-1.2's compatible_licences against the project's configured output licence, naming the specific overlap in the finding's alternative_explanation. Still does NOT auto-resolve to GREEN -- confirming the actual Article-5 merge remains a human question -- so the underlying limitation is narrowed, not eliminated.
